question: In 1995, physicists Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman created the first Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) using which isotope?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rubidium-87**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman**, two physicists, achieved a remarkable breakthrough in **1995** by creating the first Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC).
 
• The Bose-Einstein condensate was formed using the isotope **Rubidium-87**. This isotope was chosen for its suitable atomic properties that allowed cooling down to extremely low temperatures.
 
• **Bose-Einstein condensates** occur when a group of bosonic atoms is cooled to temperatures close to absolute zero, where they occupy the lowest quantum state and behave like a single entity.
 
• Rubidium-87 is a bosonic isotope because its atomic nucleus has an **integer spin**, making it ideal for Bose-Einstein condensation.
 
• To create the BEC, Cornell and Wieman used advanced techniques, including **laser cooling** and **magnetic trapping**, to achieve temperatures below **170 nanokelvin**.
 
• This achievement proved the theoretical predictions made by **Satyendra Nath Bose** and **Albert Einstein** decades earlier regarding the behavior of bosonic particles at near-zero temperatures.
 
• The creation of the Bose-Einstein condensate marked a major milestone in quantum mechanics and opened new avenues for research in fields such as **quantum computing** and **precision measurement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rubidium-87:**

 
 
• **Rubidium** is a chemical element with symbol **Rb** and atomic number **37**. Rubidium-87 is one of its naturally occurring isotopes.
 
• This isotope is widely used in atomic physics experiments due to its favorable properties for cooling and trapping.
 
 
 
• **Bose-Einstein Condensates:**
 
 
• BECs are formed by cooling bosonic atoms to temperatures close to absolute zero, at which quantum effects become macroscopic.
 
• Such condensates are used in research on superfluidity, quantum simulations, and the study of fundamental quantum phenomena.
 
 
 
• **Other isotopes considered for Bose-Einstein condensation:**
 
 
• Although **Sodium-23** was used in later experiments, Rubidium-87 was the first isotope successfully condensed into a BEC.
 
• Other isotopes, such as **Cesium-133** and **Thorium-232**, have different atomic properties, making them less suitable for BEC formation under the conditions used by Cornell and Wieman.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satyendra Nath Bose and Albert Einstein:**

 
 
• The Bose-Einstein condensate was first predicted theoretically by **Satyendra Nath Bose** and **Albert Einstein** in the 1920s.
 
• They proposed that at extremely low temperatures, bosonic particles would collapse into the same quantum state, forming a condensate.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Bose-Einstein Condensates:**
 
 
• BECs are used for research in **quantum mechanics**, **quantum computing**, and **precision measurements**.
 
• The study of BECs has enabled advancements in understanding phenomena such as **superfluidity** and **quantum phase transitions**.
